extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news innovators, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and norms for highlighting, analyzing, and sharing journalistic innovations and practices that help journalism survive and thrive in the Internet age; also includes site reuse/licensing and fellowship procedural notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting and analyzing innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab aims to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We want to find good ideas for others to steal. The Lab’s work focuses on identifying innovations in the news ecosystem, diagnosing success/failure factors, and explaining what can be learned and replicated by others (startups, traditional news organizations, reporters, and editors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical help for reporters and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors and help traditional news organizations find a way to survive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage and recommendations should be oriented toward usable guidance: tactics, workflows, and business approaches that allow practitioners to adapt to the radically changed online news environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center reader contributions and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among [our resources] are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab solicits and values reader-submitted accounts of what's happening or what should happen; content and analysis are meant to be interactive and informed by practitioner and reader input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watchdog journalism encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project encourages reporters and editors to monitor and hold accountable those who exert power in all aspects of public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the Lab/Foundation’s remit, watchdog work is framed as an essential journalistic function — monitoring power structures and promoting accountability is a criterion for coverage and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership and default rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default ownership is reserved; any reuse should respect the indicated copyright unless a specific alternative notice appears with the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 US license terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, site content is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses include translating, transforming, reprinting, or otherwise reusing content provided that (a) the use is noncommercial and (b) attribution is given to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the work’s author, preferably with a link back to the original content. Examples given: translating the site into another language; redistributing posts for a college course; reusing the Twitter feed as lyrics. For any other (commercial or unusual) uses, contact the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowship application timing (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Foundation administers a midcareer fellowship program; the annual deadline to apply is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural/eligibility-related deadline for applicants to the fellowship program (described as a year of study and exploration at Harvard for accomplished journalists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial stance: optimism and experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab states 'We are fundamentally optimistic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site’s editorial voice favors experimentation and constructive analysis: coverage prioritizes projects and ideas that explore new business models, technologies, and practices with an eye toward practical potential rather than cynicism.
